title: Zix CLI
headline: From an API specification to an explicit command.
summary: A Rust dispatcher owns specification review and integrity checks; providers own transport and authentication. The released binary makes that boundary inspectable.
alt: Recorded local output from the released Zix CLI

sections.title: The dispatcher boundary
sections.text: Separate specification input, explicitly selected operations, source hashes and provider execution contracts. The recorded run parses a synthetic OpenAPI document and extracts the GET /inspection route.

sections.title: Verification with a released binary
sections.text: Run version, api project and api routes with v0.2.2 and retain actual inputs and outputs in examples/zix. The observation uses no credential, external request or live data mutation. Group-writable catalog input was refused as designed.

title: NuxtJP
headline: Developer experience, from the first visit.
summary: Nuxt itself and community-built tools serve different needs. The interface separates learning the framework from choosing a NuxtJP package.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.text: A shared Nuxt foundation handles locale and static generation. Site-owned components and typed content own navigation, visual identity and the visitor journey. This keeps shared infrastructure from flattening every site into the same template.

sections.title: Verification
sections.text: The released interface was checked in English and Japanese at 360, 768 and 1440 pixels, including menu control, image loading and primary destinations. Version-tagged CI binds the source commit to the static archive before deployment.

title: iHAT
headline: Turn a release list into a useful decision.
summary: Finding a HAT starts with what it does. Search, purpose filters and version-specific exits make a catalog usable without hiding the release identity.

sections.title: The interaction
sections.text: Eight public HAT releases are grouped by purpose. Search and category filtering run in the browser over the published catalog, including an honest empty-result state.

sections.title: Verification
sections.text: The live catalog was checked for narrowing search results, category selection and empty results. English and Japanese views retain the same eight versioned release destinations.

title: sem-lang
headline: Explain meaning before exposing an API.
summary: A language tool needs a concrete example before a specification. The site introduces input, context, interpretation and unresolved questions as one readable sequence.
category: An interface for a technical concept

sections.title: Architecture
sections.text: Presentation copy and route definitions are typed and validated before static generation. Public source releases and per-file license notices remain the authoritative implementation reference.

sections.title: Verification
sections.text: The deployed site, source-release destination and MPL license entry were checked in both languages. Release artifacts are source-bound, while domain and preview settings are verified during deployment.
